title: Move two sterile medicine cups onto a sterile field with thumb forceps: only their tips may touch, no arm over the field
instruction: Using the sterile forceps, move both medicine cups from the opened sterile pack onto the sterile field without contaminating anything, then lay the forceps back across the field's edge and let go.
context: Registered nurses (O*NET 29-1141.00; 3,465,400 employed in 2025; "Prepare rooms, sterile instruments, equipment, or supplies and ensure that stock of supplies is maintained.") and medical assistants (O*NET 31-9092.00; 833,900 employed in 2025), who prepare treatment rooms and hand physicians instruments and materials, set up a sterile field with bare hands before they glove. Sterile forceps are then the only thing that may touch sterile supplies. Doyle and McCutcheon, Clinical Procedures for Safer Patient Care (1.5, principles of sterile technique), gives the rules scored here: "Place large items on the sterile field using sterile gloves or sterile transfer forceps"; "the border of one inch at the edge of the sterile drape is considered non-sterile"; "a non-sterile person should not reach over a sterile field"; "Keep the tips of forceps down". The robot's grippers are the bare hands: it has to work the forceps as a tool and reach in from the edge.
setup: Cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x away from the robot, y left; heights above the table, which stands in for a treatment-room counter. Sterile field, fixed: a stainless Mayo instrument tray (49 x 32.5 x 1.9 cm) under a blue sterile drape, a block 32.5 (x) by 49 (y) by 2.0 cm, near edge at x 33.0, y -17.0 to 32.0. Sterile pack, fixed: an opened sterilization wrapper, light blue, 30.5 x 30.5 cm, 2 mm thick, lying flat, inside up, near edge at x 33.0, y -51.5 to -21.0. Two stainless-steel 2 oz (59 ml) graduated medicine cups, loose: 5.1 cm across the rolled rim, 4.45 cm tall, 3.7 cm across the base, 35 g; they stand on the pack with their middles at (38.5, -34.5) and (38.5, -44.0). Sterile thumb dressing forceps, loose: stainless, 14 cm (5.5 in), serrated tips, 25 g, tips 15 mm apart at rest, about 2.5 N at the finger grip to close them. They lie on edge (the two blades side by side, 11 mm tall) along x at y -11.5: tail at x 28.0, so the handle sticks 5 cm out over the field's near edge, tips at x 42.0 on the field. Both arms start in their rest pose; no part of them is over the field or the pack. Second layout (XFER_LOT=B): cups at (39.5, -32.0) and (38.5, -42.0), forceps at y -10.5. Sterile: the cups, the 5 cm of the forceps from their tips, and the tops of the field and the pack more than 2.5 cm from their edges. Not sterile: the grippers and arms, the table, both 2.5 cm borders, the tray's sides, and the 6.5 cm of the forceps from their tail.
scoring: Scored at the end from what touched what during the trial (video, and a ruler for the borders). Touching means within 1.5 mm; 4 mm for any part of an arm. A sterile thing is contaminated when it touches the table, a 2.5 cm border, the tray's side, an arm, the forceps' handle (the 6.5 cm from the tail) or anything already contaminated. The field or the pack is also contaminated when any part of an arm is above its sterile part at any height; the forceps' working end (the 5 cm from the tips) also when, while the forceps are held (an arm within 3 cm of them), the tips are more than 5 mm higher than the handle's end. 0 if the field is contaminated. Otherwise 0.25 for one cup and 0.5 for both that stand on the field's sterile part (upright within 10 degrees, the whole cup inside the border), uncontaminated, let go (arms 3 cm away, forceps' tips 2 cm away) and at rest (under 2 cm/s). 0.75: both cups, and the forceps put down, let go (arms 3 cm away) and at rest. 1.0: both cups, and the forceps put down uncontaminated with their whole working end resting on the sterile part of the field or the pack.
reset_notes: Stand the cups on their marks on the pack and lay the forceps across the field's edge. Nothing is consumed; on a real rig the cups, forceps, drape and wrapper are treated as sterile by convention at the start of each trial.
fidelity: Rigid parts at full size. Forceps: two bowed steel blades on a sprung hinge at the tail; the closing force, blade thickness, cup wall (0.8 mm) and both masses are estimates. Drape and wrapper are flat rigid surfaces: no cloth, no fluid. Touching is judged by distance, once per control step, over the arms' whole collision shapes. A gripper pad meets a blade over a 4 mm patch (soft rubber). Not tried on a physical rig.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; demo: 1.0 (the demo video shows the overhead camera beside the right wrist camera)
